lotl.body: The Leafs' season is in the books at 32-36-14, and the conversation has moved squarely to what comes next. They finished 8th in atlantic division - a final placement that frames every decision this summer. The work now runs through the draft table, the trade market and the cap sheet, and the bets made over the next few weeks will shape the roster that shows up to camp. The next headline here comes from the front office, not the scoreboard. The NHL calendar has flipped to building season - draft prep, trade talks, and the roster surgery that shapes the next contending window. For the Toronto Maple Leafs, the work runs from the draft table to the trade market, and the choices made this summer will define the next window.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The bruise from Tuesday night is fresh, and it shows in the ledger as much as the mood. The Blue Jays' 7-4 loss to the Phillies on June 10 dropped them to 33-36, left them third in the AL East and 9 games back - hardly the posture of a club with the luxury of waste. The sting is that the night carried a milestone and a cautionary tale at once: Max Scherzer reached 3,500 strikeouts, but the headline in the end was the same old problem - too many cracks, not enough clean innings. Toronto answered with a 3-2 win Monday and a 6-4 victory over Baltimore on June 7, so there is still some pulse here, but the current is weak, a one-game skid in a season that keeps slipping just out of reach. The next turn comes fast. Toronto gets the Yankees on Friday at 6:37 p.m. ET, and if it wants to matter in June, it had better start playing like it knows it.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The season ended with a little more promise than most rebuilding clubs can claim - and still enough doubt to keep Toronto honest. The Raptors finished 46-36, third in the Atlantic Division, and the year closed with a win that left them one step short of the league's second round. That matters because this was not a collapse; it was a club that got back to the playoffs for the first time since 2022 and showed enough backbone to suggest the foundation is real. But the hard part starts now. The center spot remains the clearest hole, and the fresh chatter around budget-friendly targets only underlines how tight the margin is for a team that has to spend carefully. The broader question is whether this roster needs a tweak or a turn - whether the next move is a sensible free-agent fit, a draft swing, or a more serious reshaping of the front of the bench. What Toronto does at center - and whether it keeps building around this core - will define the summer.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: Something is taking shape in Ashburn, and it is not another sleepy June tableau. Joshua Josephs has pushed his way into the conversation during the final week of OTAs - the kind of late-arriving edge presence that can turn a roster battle from polite to ruthless. Washington is still listed third in the NFC East, but that record is history now; the real business is who sticks, who learns fast, and who looks ready to help Jayden Daniels when the hits start to count again. Luke McCaffrey, the forgotten receiver, is forcing his way back onto the page, while Mikey Sainristil is drawing the sort of early buzz that usually comes with a bigger role and a shorter leash. That is how June works for a team trying to sharpen its identity: one good week can change a depth chart, and one quiet week can send a player back to the margins. Brandon Aiyuk's situation is making Washington's decision easier by the day, too. What happens next in minicamp will tell us whether these names are camp chatter or the first draft of a sharper, faster Commanders offense.
